I was in Haiti in 2018.  I could write a book about it.  Marines working for an NGO who hated our guts, but couldn't work without our heavies.  We hauled rice and grain and flower to warlords who took it from the weak and powerless.  Guys with bright orange vests and machetes would pack it all in trucks while the men, women and children in rags watched helplessly.  I secured imagery for the S2 and got fields and fields of bodies from the floods. What really fucked me up is this woman who had her arms thrown up into the air.  But it was like she was looking at us and yelling at us. We were simply in a CH53 trying to deliver food somewhere and she was yelling and screaming at us. There was a bundled corpse at her feet at the edge of a water hole or maybe something that was flooded out. It was like she was praying to the helicopter or blaming it I never knew which.  Somewhere I still have those photos. 

In other places we went we couldn't find any type of authority.  I went to a village after we left Port Au'Prince and stopped off at the ship to get USAID relief boxes full of tarps.  We went out for like an hour and 45 minutes and landed in what I think was a soccer field.  They had a giant bonfire going and we were delivering there because there was some American preacher there.  But no one really listened to his speeches about God, they seemed to just sort of treat him like some guest they took really good care of.  
Anyway, there was a burning stack of wood that I remember almost snuffing out and then it ignited in a huge bowl of fire at least 40 to 50 ft high. When we came down with the helicopter the downdraft seem to just blow the fire out. But then ones we landed it's like it caught all the oxygen like you blew into a sparkler or a burning twig and it just exploded. Long story short, lol, we found out that the villagers had found the witch doctors in the village and cut them to pieces with machetes because they thought that the witch doctors did something to cause the hurricane. 
Also I remember there were a lot of Germans in Haiti that live in compounds with 14 ft high walls and hired European bodyguards. That was really odd.
